classification.difficultyReason: Identify the quadrant containing each positive angle within one revolution.

questions.mappingNote: Each part directly assesses identifying a quadrant from its angular interval; astc-sign-of-ratio is the closest supplied skill.
questions.methodNote: Measure positive angles anticlockwise from the positive x-axis. The quadrants are numbered anticlockwise, with boundaries at 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the quadrant containing each positive angle within one revolution.

classification.difficultyReason: Find each acute related angle and combine it with the quadrant sign to rewrite the ratio without evaluation.

questions.mappingNote: Each of the nine expressions requires exactly the related-angle method demonstrated in Example 3. The primary skill is related-angles; quadrant-sign identification supports it.
questions.methodNote: Example 3 on pages 8–9 finds the acute related angle, identifies the quadrant and attaches the appropriate sign without evaluating the acute-angle ratio. Page 7 supplies the related-angle rules; pages 3–4 establish quadrant signs and tangent as sine over cosine.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find each acute related angle and combine it with the quadrant sign to rewrite the ratio without evaluation.

classification.difficultyReason: Combine the related angle, quadrant sign and an exact acute-angle ratio.

questions.mappingNote: All nine parts directly assess exact ratios for second-, third- or fourth-quadrant angles. The quadrant-forms skill is the closest primary match; exact acute ratios and related angles support it.
questions.methodNote: Use the related angle, determine the sign from the quadrant, then substitute the exact acute-angle ratio, following Example 4 on PDF page 9.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine the related angle, quadrant sign and an exact acute-angle ratio.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught sign chart to select the quadrant satisfying each pair of ratio signs.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts directly assess identifying a quadrant from trigonometric signs; astc-sign-of-ratio is the closest catalogue skill.
questions.methodNote: Use unit-circle coordinate signs for sine and cosine, and the taught tangent sign rule obtained from tan θ = sin θ / cos θ. Intersect the quadrants satisfying the two conditions.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply the taught sign chart to select the quadrant satisfying each pair of ratio signs.

classification.difficultyReason: Use unit-circle coordinates to evaluate quadrantal ratios and explain undefined tangent values.

questions.mappingNote: The directly assessed skill is evaluating trigonometric ratios at multiples of 90°, including explaining undefined tangent. Unit-circle definitions and the tangent quotient support the construction and explanation.
questions.methodNote: Read cosine and sine as the x- and y-coordinates of P on the unit circle; calculate tangent as sine divided by cosine. Page 4 explicitly gives the four axial coordinates and excludes tangent at 90° and 270°.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Use unit-circle coordinates to evaluate quadrantal ratios and explain undefined tangent values.

classification.difficultyReason: Combine exact ratios obtained from related angles, quadrant signs and unit-circle axis values.

questions.mappingNote: Each part combines exact trigonometric values. Parts a and d use second-quadrant 45-degree ratios; b and c use fourth-quadrant 30-degree ratios; e uses third-quadrant 45-degree ratios; f uses third- and fourth-quadrant 60-degree ratios. Axis values are also needed in a, b, c and e.
questions.methodNote: Use unit-circle coordinates for axis values, tangent as sine over cosine, the acute related angle and quadrant signs, then substitute exact special-angle values and simplify.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine exact ratios obtained from related angles, quadrant signs and unit-circle axis values.

classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate exact ratios with quadrant signs before squaring and adding.

questions.mappingNote: Exact-ratio evaluation is directly assessed; the identity is developed in the following question.
questions.methodNote: Use the exact-value table, related angles and quadrant signs, then square the ratios.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Evaluate exact ratios with quadrant signs before squaring and adding.

classification.difficultyReason: Prove the identity and explain its extension to other quadrants and axis angles.

questions.mappingNote: The complete task establishes the Pythagorean identity across quadrants.
questions.methodNote: Use right-triangle ratios and Pythagoras, then unit-circle signs and axis coordinates.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Prove the identity and explain its extension to other quadrants and axis angles.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply reciprocal definitions to signed exact trigonometric values.

questions.mappingNote: Finding exact reciprocal ratios is the most advanced directly assessed skill.
questions.methodNote: Use the embedded reciprocal definitions with exact ratios, related angles and quadrant signs.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply reciprocal definitions to signed exact trigonometric values.

classification.difficultyReason: Derive an identity by division and identify angles where its functions are undefined.

questions.mappingNote: The requested proof and domain restriction directly assess Pythagorean identities.
questions.methodNote: Use the Pythagorean identity established in question 8, divide by cosine squared, then apply the tangent quotient and secant reciprocal definitions.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Derive an identity by division and identify angles where its functions are undefined.

classification.difficultyReason: Combine exact related angles with quadrant reasoning and draw a diagram for every equation.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts solve exact trigonometric equations over the inclusive interval; each explicitly requires a diagram.
questions.methodNote: Use ASTC or a unit-circle diagram to identify quadrants, identify the exact acute related angle, and calculate both angles as in Example 5 on page 12.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine exact related angles with quadrant reasoning and draw a diagram for every equation.

classification.difficultyReason: Find exact solutions using quadrants and include axis and interval-endpoint solutions.

questions.mappingNote: The task solves exact trigonometric equations, including special axis values and both inclusive endpoints in part f.
questions.methodNote: Use exact acute ratios and ASTC as in Example 5; use the unit-circle axis coordinates and tangent quotient on page 4 for parts d–f.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find exact solutions using quadrants and include axis and interval-endpoint solutions.

classification.difficultyReason: Draw quadrant diagrams, calculate acute related angles, obtain both solutions and round to the nearest degree.

questions.mappingNote: Each part directly assesses solving a numerical trigonometric equation using a related angle and the two appropriate quadrants.
questions.methodNote: Follow Example 5(c): draw the circle diagram, select quadrants from the sign, calculate the acute related angle from the positive magnitude in degree mode, and obtain both angles. Retain calculator precision until final nearest-degree rounding.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Draw quadrant diagrams, calculate acute related angles, obtain both solutions and round to the nearest degree.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply clockwise angle measurement, retaining complete turns and placing the terminal arm for each negative angle.

questions.mappingNote: The task assesses negative-angle representation rather than evaluation of a trigonometric ratio.
questions.methodNote: Measure negative angles clockwise from the positive x-axis; adding full revolutions identifies the terminal arm without changing the direction of the requested drawing.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply clockwise angle measurement, retaining complete turns and placing the terminal arm for each negative angle.

classification.difficultyReason: Use the terminal arms already constructed in question 1 to read their angles to the x-axis, including zero for axis-terminal cases.

questions.mappingNote: This separately numbered source task refers explicitly to question 1 and remains its own whole-question block as directed by the repair decision.
questions.methodNote: Reduce by complete revolutions, then use the angle between the terminal arm and the x-axis. Although page 6 defines the related angle as acute, the matched teacher answers explicitly extend the convention to 0 degrees for these axis-terminal cases.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Use the terminal arms already constructed in question 1 to read their angles to the x-axis, including zero for axis-terminal cases.

classification.difficultyReason: Use the clockwise rotations already drawn in question 2 to identify the angle between each terminal arm and the x-axis.

questions.mappingNote: This independently numbered source task retains its explicit reference to question 2 and starts its own alphabetical part sequence.
questions.methodNote: Add full revolutions to identify the terminal arm, then find its angle to the x-axis. Teacher question 4 confirms the 0-degree convention for terminal arms on the x-axis.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Use the clockwise rotations already drawn in question 2 to identify the angle between each terminal arm and the x-axis.

classification.difficultyReason: Combine removal of complete revolutions with quadrant signs and exact trigonometric values.

questions.mappingNote: Related-angle reduction is the most advanced directly assessed operation; the printed Example 6 reference is retained in the prompt.
questions.methodNote: Follow Example 6: subtract complete revolutions, identify the quadrant and related angle, then apply the exact-value table or unit-circle axis values.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine removal of complete revolutions with quadrant signs and exact trigonometric values.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert negative angles to coterminal positive angles and use quadrant signs with exact values.

questions.mappingNote: Use coterminal-angle reduction as taught here rather than substituting later negative-angle identities. Preserve the printed Example 7 reference.
questions.methodNote: Follow Example 7: add a suitable multiple of 360 degrees, identify the quadrant and related angle, then evaluate exactly with the appropriate sign.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert negative angles to coterminal positive angles and use quadrant signs with exact values.

classification.difficultyReason: Reduce positive and negative rotations to coterminal axis angles, then evaluate the requested ratio using unit-circle coordinates or the tangent quotient.

questions.mappingNote: All parts terminate on coordinate axes, making evaluation at multiples of 90 degrees the primary skill.
questions.methodNote: Reduce to a coterminal angle within one revolution. Read sine and cosine from unit-circle coordinates; tangent is sine divided by cosine.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Reduce positive and negative rotations to coterminal axis angles, then evaluate the requested ratio using unit-circle coordinates or the tangent quotient.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct a first-quadrant value table and use symmetry to complete a sine graph over one revolution.

questions.mappingNote: The task directly assesses constructing a sine graph from a first-quadrant table and extending it by symmetry; graph-trig-functions is the closest supplied skill.
questions.methodNote: Page 15 introduces the sine coordinate and its changes by quadrant. Page 16 builds a value table, plots the sine graph and establishes reflection symmetry. Page 17 combines the related-angle symmetries and describes periodic extension. Page 18 supplies the assigned instruction and the analogous cosine construction.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct a first-quadrant value table and use symmetry to complete a sine graph over one revolution.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct a cosine value table and extend the plotted first-quadrant values using symmetry.

questions.mappingNote: Question 2 directly assesses the demonstrated table-to-cosine-graph method, using ten-degree increments and symmetry.
questions.methodNote: The source develops sine from unit-circle values, tables and symmetry, then applies the same process to cosine. Pages 17–18 show cosine's quadrant behaviour, a value table and its complete graph.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct a cosine value table and extend the plotted first-quadrant values using symmetry.

classification.difficultyReason: Read ordinates, find two intersections with a horizontal level, and identify intersections of two trigonometric curves.

questions.mappingNote: The most advanced assessed task is solving equations graphically, including equality of two functions. Direct graph reading supports the earlier parts.
questions.methodNote: Pages 15–18 develop sine and cosine graphs from unit-circle coordinates, tables and symmetry. Read function values as ordinates at a given angle; read solutions from the angles at a horizontal level; equality corresponds to curve intersections. No inverse-trigonometric shortcut is used.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Read ordinates, find two intersections with a horizontal level, and identify intersections of two trigonometric curves.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the sine graph's extreme values and the angles at which they recur.

questions.mappingNote: Both parts assess interpretation of the sine graph and its periodicity, matching graph-trig-functions.
questions.methodNote: Read the highest and lowest ordinates of the sine graph. PDF page 16 gives the sine table and graph with extrema at 90° and 270°; PDF page 17 extends the graph and establishes its 360° period.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the sine graph's extreme values and the angles at which they recur.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the extrema of the standard cosine graph and use its period to describe their locations.

questions.mappingNote: Both parts assess properties of the standard cosine graph. Periodicity gives all locations of the extrema, consistent with the teacher key.
questions.methodNote: Read maximum and minimum ordinates from the cosine graph. Page 17 describes its changes through the four quadrants; page 18 supplies the cosine graph and its 360-degree period.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the extrema of the standard cosine graph and use its period to describe their locations.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct diagrams connecting related-angle cosine identities with unit-circle coordinates and cosine-graph symmetry.

questions.mappingNote: All three parts directly assess cosine relationships for quadrant forms; unit-circle definitions and graph symmetry support the requested diagrams.
questions.methodNote: Cosine is the unit-circle horizontal coordinate. Use reflection in the vertical axis, a half-turn about the origin and reflection in the horizontal axis, then illustrate the corresponding equal or opposite cosine-graph ordinates.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct diagrams connecting related-angle cosine identities with unit-circle coordinates and cosine-graph symmetry.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct unit-circle diagrams and interpret reflected coordinates to illustrate two negative-angle identities.

questions.mappingNote: Both parts directly assess the negative-angle relationships through diagrams, with the unit-circle coordinate definitions supplying the justification.
questions.methodNote: Use cosine and sine as the x- and y-coordinates on the unit circle. Positive and negative rotations place corresponding points on opposite sides of the x-axis. Reflection preserves x and reverses y. The symmetry and periodicity discussion supports interpreting negative angles.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct unit-circle diagrams and interpret reflected coordinates to illustrate two negative-angle identities.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct a table at 15-degree intervals and use it to sketch a sine function with two cycles and amplitude 3.

questions.mappingNote: The directly assessed task is constructing a trigonometric graph from calculated values. Amplitude and period changes support graph-trig-functions, with transform-trig-functions secondary.
questions.methodNote: PDF page 16 explicitly constructs a sine table, plots the points and joins them with a smooth curve. Pages 15–17 explain sine coordinates, symmetry and periodicity; page 18 repeats table-to-graph construction for cosine. Apply the table method to 3 sin(2 theta), evaluating each doubled angle in degrees.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct a table at 15-degree intervals and use it to sketch a sine function with two cycles and amplitude 3.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct a table at 15-degree intervals and sketch two cycles of a scaled cosine function.

questions.mappingNote: The whole task directly assesses constructing a cosine graph from a value table; scaling and the doubled angle support the graph-trig-functions classification.
questions.methodNote: Pages 16 and 18 demonstrate calculating a trigonometric value table, plotting the points and joining them with a smooth curve. Pages 17–18 explain periodicity and cosine symmetry. Apply that table-and-plot method to 4cos(2θ), evaluating the doubled angles in degrees.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct a table at 15-degree intervals and sketch two cycles of a scaled cosine function.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Isolate a trigonometric ratio, identify its exact related angle and select both solutions in the specified interval.

classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange linear trigonometric equations, calculate related angles and select both solutions using quadrant signs.

questions.methodNote: Use degree mode, isolate the trigonometric ratio, calculate the acute related angle, then select the quadrants from the ratio's sign, as in Example 9. Retain calculator precision until the final nearest-degree answers.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Rearrange linear trigonometric equations, calculate related angles and select both solutions using quadrant signs.

classification.difficultyReason: Take both square roots and use exact related angles to find four solutions in the restricted domain.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts directly apply Example 10; parts e and f first divide by the coefficient. Exact values follow the table on page 6, with quadrant signs supported by page 4.
questions.methodNote: Example 10 isolates the squared ratio, takes positive and negative square roots, identifies the exact related angle and selects solutions in all four quadrants.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Take both square roots and use exact related angles to find four solutions in the restricted domain.

classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied quotient identity, rearrange part b, then select both quadrants for a positive exact tangent value.

questions.mappingNote: Page 4 defines tangent as sine over cosine and gives its positive quadrants; page 6 supplies exact tangent values. Pages 20–21 teach algebraic isolation followed by related angles and quadrant selection. Solving the equations is the most advanced directly assessed skill.
questions.methodNote: Use the supplied sine-over-cosine identity to isolate tangent, identify an exact related angle, and choose every applicable quadrant in the stated interval.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Use the supplied quotient identity, rearrange part b, then select both quadrants for a positive exact tangent value.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify acute related angles, first rewriting angles outside one revolution where necessary.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–d directly identify related angles; e–h first use the equivalent-angle method demonstrated on page 14. The assessed result in every part is a related angle.
questions.methodNote: Use the acute angle between the terminal radius and the x-axis. In quadrants II, III and IV use 180°−θ, θ−180° and 360°−θ respectively. For angles outside one revolution, add or subtract 360° first.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify acute related angles, first rewriting angles outside one revolution where necessary.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply exact acute-angle ratios and quadrant signs to find three ratios for each angle.

questions.mappingNote: All eight parts directly apply quadrant-form relationships to exact acute-angle ratios; no equation solving or calculator approximation is assessed.
questions.methodNote: Find the acute related angle, determine each ratio's sign using its quadrant, then apply the exact 30°, 45° or 60° ratio. Page 4 supplies ASTC and the tangent quotient; page 6 supplies the exact-value table; pages 7–8 demonstrate related angles and signs.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply exact acute-angle ratios and quadrant signs to find three ratios for each angle.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute given angles, distinguish multiples of angles from multiples of ratios, and evaluate exact values using quadrant signs.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a and c evaluate the doubled angle before applying a ratio; parts b and d multiply an exact ratio by two. Part e substitutes and squares the exact ratios directly, without requiring a double-angle identity. Parts c and f use second-quadrant signs and acute related angles.
questions.methodNote: Page 6 supplies exact sine, cosine and tangent values for 30°, 45° and 60°. Page 7 demonstrates related-angle evaluation with quadrant signs. Page 4 explains the signs of tangent through sine divided by cosine.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute given angles, distinguish multiples of angles from multiples of ratios, and evaluate exact values using quadrant signs.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct a value table and graph two complete sine cycles over the specified interval.

questions.mappingNote: Apply the same value-table method to the argument 2θ. Values at 45-degree increments identify all zeros and turning points, and show two complete sine cycles.
questions.methodNote: Page 16 constructs the sine graph from a value table and joins plotted points smoothly; page 17 explains periodicity. Page 18 repeats the table-and-plot procedure for cosine. Pages 4 and 6 support the axis values and exact sine values used here.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct a value table and graph two complete sine cycles over the specified interval.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct a value table and plot two complete cycles of a cosine function with a doubled angle.

questions.mappingNote: Question 5 applies this table-and-plot method to cosine with argument 2θ. Evaluating at 45-degree intervals in θ gives exact zeros and turning points across two cycles.
questions.methodNote: Pages 16 and 18 construct trigonometric graphs by tabulating values, plotting points and drawing a smooth curve. Pages 17–18 explain periodicity; pages 4 and 6 supply axis-angle and exact-ratio values.

classification.difficultyReason: Use exact related angles and quadrant signs to find every solution; the final part requires both square roots.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–e apply exact related angles and quadrant signs to enumerate solutions on the closed interval. Part f matches the squared-sine method of Example 10, including both square roots and all four quadrants.
questions.methodNote: Page 4 supplies quadrant signs; page 6 supplies exact ratios; page 7 explains related angles. Page 20 Example 8 solves using the related angle and the appropriate quadrants. Page 21 Example 10 explicitly takes both signs when solving a squared sine equation.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Use exact related angles and quadrant signs to find every solution; the final part requires both square roots.

classification.difficultyReason: Reduce positive and negative angles to one revolution, then combine quadrant signs with exact related-angle ratios.

questions.methodNote: Page 14 teaches subtracting or adding multiples of 360 degrees to obtain an equivalent angle within one revolution; Examples 6 and 7 then use a related angle and quadrant sign. Pages 4 and 7 establish signs and related angles, and page 6 supplies exact ratios.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Reduce positive and negative angles to one revolution, then combine quadrant signs with exact related-angle ratios.

classification.difficultyReason: Find a calculator related angle and use the appropriate quadrants to obtain both solutions to the nearest degree.

classification.difficultyReason: Isolate a trigonometric ratio and identify every exact solution in an inclusive revolution, including axis endpoints.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–d apply the linear-equation method with exact related angle 60 degrees. Parts e–f use the axis values after isolating the ratio. The inclusive domain requires retaining both 0 degrees and 360 degrees in part f.
questions.methodNote: Page 20 Example 8 isolates the trigonometric ratio, finds the related angle and uses its sign to select quadrants. Page 21 Example 9 reinforces that sequence. Page 6 supplies exact special-angle ratios; page 4 supplies quadrant signs and unit-circle axis values.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Isolate a trigonometric ratio and identify every exact solution in an inclusive revolution, including axis endpoints.

classification.difficultyReason: Combine squared exact ratios and reciprocal ratios across several quadrants, retaining the signs of all three terms.

questions.mappingNote: The task combines exact ordinary and reciprocal ratios at specified angles. Exact reciprocal ratios is the most advanced directly assessed skill; related angles and axial values supply the constituent values.
questions.methodNote: Page 4 supplies axial sine/cosine values and quadrant signs; page 6 gives exact special-angle ratios; page 7 develops related angles. Page 11 explicitly defines squared-ratio notation and cosecant, secant and cotangent as reciprocals. Page 14 demonstrates exact-value substitution using related angles; page 16 corroborates the sine values at 120° and 270°.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine squared exact ratios and reciprocal ratios across several quadrants, retaining the signs of all three terms.

classification.difficultyReason: Reduce angles exceeding one revolution, substitute exact ratios and combine surd fractions to establish the supplied equality.

questions.mappingNote: Both reduced angles lie in the first quadrant. Direct substitution of exact ratios proves the equality using taught methods without requiring a sum identity.
questions.methodNote: Page 6 supplies exact sine and cosine values for 45° and 60°. Page 14 explains subtracting multiples of 360° and demonstrates exact evaluation in Example 6. Pages 4 and 7 establish quadrant signs; page 12 demonstrates reference-angle reasoning.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Reduce angles exceeding one revolution, substitute exact ratios and combine surd fractions to establish the supplied equality.

classification.difficultyReason: Determine quarter-cycle points and periods for three explicitly specified sine functions, then coordinate their sketches on shared axes with excluded endpoints.

questions.mappingNote: Apply the taught sine-graph construction to theta, 2theta and 3theta. Their successive quarter-cycle points occur every 90, 45 and 30 degrees respectively; the assessed task is graphing and comparing periods.
questions.methodNote: Pages 16–17 construct the sine graph from known values, symmetry and periodic repetition. Page 18 reinforces plotting values and using symmetry. Exact values on page 6 and the unit-circle bounds on page 4 support the key points.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Determine quarter-cycle points and periods for three explicitly specified sine functions, then coordinate their sketches on shared axes with excluded endpoints.

classification.difficultyReason: Rewrite reciprocal and quotient ratios, preserve domain restrictions, then factor a quadratic in sine without losing zero solutions.

questions.mappingNote: The main assessed step is reduction to and factorisation of a quadratic in sine. Apply the taught sine range to reject sine equal to 2 and the unit-circle axis values to retain both interval endpoints.
questions.methodNote: Page 4 supplies tangent as sine over cosine, its excluded angles, the sine range and axis values. Pages 20–21 teach algebraic reduction of trigonometric equations and finding every solution in the stated domain, including equations involving squared sine. The reciprocal secant definition is required to reduce this challenge.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Rewrite reciprocal and quotient ratios, preserve domain restrictions, then factor a quadratic in sine without losing zero solutions.

classification.difficultyReason: Constructs a reciprocal graph from cosine, identifying excluded angles, asymptotes and corresponding branches.

questions.mappingNote: The most advanced directly assessed skill is graphing the reciprocal function from its underlying cosine graph. The supplied teaching images establish cosine plotting but do not explicitly define secant.
questions.methodNote: Pages 17–18 develop cosine by coordinate values, plotting and symmetry; page 18 supplies its full-revolution graph. The reciprocal construction uses sec(theta)=1/cos(theta), with zeros of cosine determining the vertical asymptotes.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Constructs a reciprocal graph from cosine, identifying excluded angles, asymptotes and corresponding branches.

classification.difficultyReason: Constructs cosecant from sine, identifying undefined angles, asymptotes and the two reciprocal branches.

questions.mappingNote: The most advanced directly assessed skill is sketching a reciprocal trigonometric graph from its underlying sine graph. The question is self-contained and does not match any supplied reuse candidate.
questions.methodNote: Page 11 defines cosecant as the reciprocal of sine. Pages 16–17 establish the sine graph using values, quadrant signs and symmetry. Construct reciprocal values, preserving sign and identifying asymptotes where sine is zero.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Constructs cosecant from sine, identifying undefined angles, asymptotes and the two reciprocal branches.

classification.difficultyReason: Factor quadratic expressions in trigonometric ratios, reject impossible roots and find every angle in the specified domain; part c first requires the Pythagorean identity.

questions.mappingNote: All three parts directly assess equations reducible to quadratics. Part a factors in cosine, part b factors in sine, and part c first replaces cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ. The supplied reuse candidates describe different original tasks and cannot be reused.
questions.methodNote: Pages 2 and 4 define the unit-circle coordinates, ratio ranges and quadrant signs. Pages 16 and 18 show exact sine and cosine values and their symmetries. Page 20 Example 8 and page 21 Examples 9–10 isolate a trigonometric ratio, identify its related angle and select every solution in the required domain. Apply this method after quadratic factorisation; part c uses the unit-circle identity cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Factor quadratic expressions in trigonometric ratios, reject impossible roots and find every angle in the specified domain; part c first requires the Pythagorean identity.

classification.difficultyReason: Connects the supplied altitude equalities to two area expressions, chooses cross-substitutions to derive the identity, then decomposes 75 degrees into known exact angles.

questions.mappingNote: Part a supplies altitude substitutions for the area comparison in part b; part c applies the resulting sine addition identity. The most advanced directly assessed skill is deriving and using a sum identity.
questions.methodNote: Page 2 connects cosine to adjacent over hypotenuse in a right triangle. Page 6 supplies exact values for 30 and 45 degrees. Question 8 itself supplies the triangle area rule and the diagram needed to derive the addition identity.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Connects the supplied altitude equalities to two area expressions, chooses cross-substitutions to derive the identity, then decomposes 75 degrees into known exact angles.

classification.difficultyReason: Recognises an exterior angle, uses the supplied unit hypotenuse to express the perpendicular height, then connects equal triangle areas to the requested identity.
